System specs:  
 GTX 970 (palit)  
 16GB RAM (can't even remember brand, but it's cheap (and bad))  
 AMD 9590 (yes, I know, silly)  
 Corsair TX750M PSU  
 250GB SSD  
 Windows 7  
  
 For a while now I've been getting crashes whenever I'm gaming - more demanding games will lead to more frequent crashes. I can play for a few minutes and then I get a black screen and the sound plays in the background for a few seconds then goes crazy and then I'm forced to hard-restart (although sometimes it does restart by itself). I have been using a back-up card instead (GTX 660ti) but it really can't handle much these days so I want to try and fix my 970. I really don't know what's causing this issue: a driver issue (reinstalled drivers multiple times with custom installation); temperature (it's not getting hot); power (just got a new PSU that should handle the load). It's only under high stress that it will crash, never crashes when browsing internet etc.  
  
 I've had a lot of problems with my pc the last two years and haven't had the money or patience to fix them, now that Corona is around I want to finally fix them. This issue must have started around this time last year after my HDD packed in and I shifted over to my SSD. It's weird as before that my pc was running fine, never any issues with the 970. My PSU also died a few months later after playing Battlefield 4 - a loud pop and a nasty smell = rip. I've recently acquired a new PSU hoping that the GPU issues would be fixed, but they haven't and I'm really hoping that the graphics card isn't dead 🙁  
  
 If I'm honest I don't even know if it's the GPU that's causing the issues, it could very well be the CPU. I don't know if shifting over to my SSD and reverting from Windows 10 to Windows 7 might have seriously messed up drivers too.  
  
 I have not tested the GPU with other rigs, and probably won't be able to.  
  
 EDIT: I don't know why I forgot to mention the fact that it doesn't ALWAYS fully crash. I can still usually control my computer, e.g. I can pause and play videos and still move around in-game and sound plays etc., but the screen has gone black (crashed GPU) and reconnecting HDMI does nothing, leading to me having to restart.  
  
 Anyways, help is much appreciated - thank you!![Image 4: :)](https://forums.tomshardware.com/data/assets/smilies/smile.gif)

 For a while now I've been getting crashes whenever I'm gaming - more demanding games will lead to more frequent crashes. I have been using a back-up card instead (GTX 660ti) but it really can't handle much these days so I want to try and fix my 970. I really don't know what's causing this issue: a driver issue (reinstalled drivers multiple times with custom installation); temperature (it's not getting hot); power (just got a new PSU that should handle the load). My PSU also died a few months later after playing Battlefield 4 - a loud pop and a nasty smell = rip. I've recently acquired a new PSU hoping that the GPU issues would be fixed, but they haven't and I'm really hoping that the graphics card isn't dead 🙁  
  
 If I'm honest I don't even know if it's the GPU that's causing the issues, it could very well be the CPU. I don't know if shifting over to my SSD and reverting from Windows 10 to Windows 7 might have seriously messed up drivers too.  
  
 I have not tested the GPU with other rigs, and probably won't be able to.

The **GeForce 900 series** is a family of [graphics processing units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphics_processing_unit "Graphics processing unit") developed by [Nvidia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia "Nvidia"), succeeding the [GeForce 700 series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_700_series "GeForce 700 series") and serving as the high-end introduction to the [Maxwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxwell_(microarchitecture) "Maxwell (microarchitecture)") microarchitecture, named after [James Clerk Maxwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Clerk_Maxwell "James Clerk Maxwell"). They were produced with [TSMC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TSMC "TSMC")'s [28 nm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/28_nm_process "28 nm process") process.

With Maxwell, the successor to [Kepler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kepler_(microarchitecture) "Kepler (microarchitecture)"), Nvidia expected three major outcomes: improved graphics capabilities, simplified programming, and better [energy efficiency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy_efficiency_(physics) "Energy efficiency (physics)") compared to the [GeForce 700 series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_700_series "GeForce 700 series") and [GeForce 600 series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_600_series "GeForce 600 series").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-Xbitlabs-9)

Maxwell was announced in September 2010,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-10) with the first Maxwell-based GeForce consumer-class products released in early 2014.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-11)

## Architecture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Architecture")]

Main article: [Maxwell (microarchitecture)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxwell_(microarchitecture) "Maxwell (microarchitecture)")

### First generation Maxwell (GM10x)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: First generation Maxwell (GM10x)")]

First generation [Maxwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxwell_(microarchitecture) "Maxwell (microarchitecture)") GM107/GM108 were released as GeForce GTX 745, GTX 750/750 Ti and GTX 850M/860M (GM107) and GT 830M/840M (GM108). These new chips provide few consumer-facing additional features; Nvidia instead focused on power efficiency. Nvidia increased the amount of L2 cache from 256 KiB on GK107 to 2 MiB on GM107, reducing the memory bandwidth needed. Accordingly, Nvidia cut the memory bus from 192 bit on GK106 to 128 bit on GM107, further saving power.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-anand750-12) Nvidia also changed the streaming multiprocessor design from that of Kepler (SMX), naming it SMM. The structure of the warp scheduler is inherited from Kepler, which allows each scheduler to issue up to two instructions that are independent from each other and are in order from the same warp. The layout of SMM units is partitioned so that each of the 4 warp schedulers in an SMM controls 1 set of 32 FP32 CUDA cores, 1 set of 8 load/store units, and 1 set of 8 special function units. This is in contrast to Kepler, where each SMX has 4 schedulers that schedule to a shared pool of 6 sets of 32 FP32 CUDA cores, 2 sets of 16 load/store units, and 2 sets of 16 special function units.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-AnandTechGTX750-13) These units are connected by a crossbar that uses power to allow the resources to be shared.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-AnandTechGTX750-13) This crossbar is removed in Maxwell.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-AnandTechGTX750-13) Texture units and FP64 CUDA cores are still shared.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-anand750-12) SMM allows for a finer-grain allocation of resources than SMX, saving power when the workload isn't optimal for shared resources. Nvidia claims a 128 CUDA core SMM has 86% of the performance of a 192 CUDA core SMX.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-anand750-12) Also, each Graphics Processing Cluster, or GPC, contains up to 4 SMX units in Kepler, and up to 5 SMM units in first generation Maxwell.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-anand750-12)

GM107 supports [CUDA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CUDA "CUDA") Compute Capability 5.0 compared to 3.5 on GK110/GK208 GPUs and 3.0 on GK10x GPUs. Dynamic Parallelism and HyperQ, two features in GK110/GK208 GPUs, are also supported across the entire Maxwell product line.

Maxwell provides native shared memory atomic operations for 32-bit integers and native shared memory 32-bit and 64-bit compare-and-swap (CAS), which can be used to implement other atomic functions.

While it was once thought that Maxwell used [tile-based immediate mode rasterization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiled_rendering "Tiled rendering"),[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-14) Nvidia corrected this at GDC 2017 saying Maxwell instead uses Tile Caching.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-15)

#### NVENC

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: NVENC")]

Main article: [Nvidia NVENC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia_NVENC "Nvidia NVENC")

Maxwell-based GPUs also contain the NVENC SIP block introduced with Kepler. Nvidia's video encoder, NVENC, is 1.5 to 2 times faster than on Kepler-based GPUs meaning it can encode video at 6 to 8 times playback speed.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-anand750-12)

#### PureVideo

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: PureVideo")]

Main article: [Nvidia PureVideo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia_PureVideo "Nvidia PureVideo")

Nvidia also claims an 8 to 10 times performance increase in [PureVideo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia_PureVideo "Nvidia PureVideo") Feature Set E video decoding due to the video decoder cache paired with increases in memory efficiency. However, [H.265](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H.265 "H.265") is not supported for full hardware decoding, relying on a mix of hardware and software decoding.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-anand750-12) When decoding video, a new low power state "GC5" is used on Maxwell GPUs to conserve power.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-anand750-12)

### Second generation Maxwell (GM20x)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Second generation Maxwell (GM20x)")]

Second generation Maxwell introduced several new technologies: Dynamic Super Resolution,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-16) Third Generation Delta Color Compression,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-international.download.nvidia.com-17) Multi-Pixel Programming Sampling,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-18) Nvidia VXGI (Real-Time-Voxel-[Global Illumination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_illumination "Global illumination")),[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-19) VR Direct,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-20)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-21)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-anandtech.com-22) Multi-Projection Acceleration,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-international.download.nvidia.com-17) and Multi-Frame Sampled Anti-Aliasing (MFAA)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-23) (however support for Coverage-Sampling Anti-Aliasing (CSAA) was removed).[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-24) HDMI 2.0 support was also added.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-25)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-26)

Second generation Maxwell also changed the ROP to memory controller ratio from 8:1 to 16:1.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-AnandTech980page3-27) However, some of the ROPs are generally idle in the GTX 970 because there are not enough enabled SMMs to give them work to do and therefore reduces its maximum fill rate.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-techreport.com-28)

Second generation upgraded [NVENC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NVENC "NVENC") which supports [HEVC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HEVC "HEVC") encoding and adds support for [H.264](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H.264 "H.264") encoding resolutions at 1440p/60FPS & 4K/60FPS compared to NVENC on Maxwell first generation GM10x GPUs which only supported H.264 1080p/60FPS encoding.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-anandtech.com-22) Maxwell GM206 GPU supports full fixed function HEVC hardware decoding.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-29)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-30)

### Async compute support

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Async compute support")]

While the Maxwell series was marketed as fully [DirectX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DirectX "DirectX") 12 compliant,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-dx12_1-2)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-980tidx12-31)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-auto-32) Oxide Games, developer of _[Ashes of the Singularity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashes\_of\_the\_Singularity "Ashes of the Singularity")_, uncovered that Maxwell-based cards do not perform well when async compute is utilized.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-33)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-oxidedx12-34)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-nvidiashim-35)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-980tidx12-31)

It appears that while this core feature is in fact exposed by the driver,[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-36) Nvidia partially implemented it through a driver-based [shim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shim_(computing) "Shim (computing)"), coming at a high performance cost.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-nvidiashim-35) Unlike AMD's competing [GCN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphics_Core_Next "Graphics Core Next")-based graphics cards which include a full implementation of hardware-based asynchronous compute,[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-37)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-38) Nvidia planned to rely on the driver to implement a software queue and a software distributor to forward asynchronous tasks to the hardware schedulers, capable of distributing the workload to the correct units.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-39) Asynchronous compute on Maxwell therefore requires that both a game and the GPU driver be specifically coded for asynchronous compute on Maxwell in order to enable this capability.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-PCPerTimeSpy-40) The 3DMark Time Spy benchmark shows no noticeable performance difference between asynchronous compute being enabled or disabled.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-PCPerTimeSpy-40) Asynchronous compute is disabled by the driver for Maxwell.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-PCPerTimeSpy-40)

Oxide claims that this led to Nvidia pressuring them not to include the asynchronous compute feature in their benchmark at all, so that the 900 series would not be at a disadvantage against AMD's products which implement asynchronous compute in hardware.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-oxidedx12-34)

Maxwell requires that the GPU be statically partitioned for asynchronous compute to allow tasks to run concurrently.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-RyanSmithDynamicScheduling-41) Each partition is assigned to a hardware queue. If any of the queues that are assigned to a partition empty out or are unable to submit work for any reason (e.g. a task in the queue must be delayed until a [hazard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hazard_(computer_architecture) "Hazard (computer architecture)") is resolved), the partition and all of the resources in that partition reserved for that queue will idle.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-RyanSmithDynamicScheduling-41) Asynchronous compute therefore could easily hurt performance on Maxwell if it is not coded to work with Maxwell's static scheduler.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-RyanSmithDynamicScheduling-41) Furthermore, graphics tasks saturate Nvidia GPUs much more easily than they do to AMD's GCN-based GPUs which are much more heavily weighted towards compute, so Nvidia GPUs have fewer scheduling holes that could be filled by asynchronous compute than AMD's.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-RyanSmithDynamicScheduling-41) For these reasons, the driver forces a Maxwell GPU to place all tasks into one queue and execute each task in serial, and give each task the undivided resources of the GPU no matter whether or not each task can saturate the GPU or not.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-RyanSmithDynamicScheduling-41)

## Advertising controversy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Advertising controversy")]

### GTX 970 hardware specifications

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: GTX 970 hardware specifications")]

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fb/NVIDIA%4028nm%40Maxwell%40GM204%40GeForce_GTX_970%40S_TAIWAN_1433A1_T4N807.M1P_GM204-200-A1_DSC04620_%2829702898116%29.jpg/250px-NVIDIA%4028nm%40Maxwell%40GM204%40GeForce_GTX_970%40S_TAIWAN_1433A1_T4N807.M1P_GM204-200-A1_DSC04620_%2829702898116%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:NVIDIA@28nm@Maxwell@GM204@GeForce_GTX_970@S_TAIWAN_1433A1_T4N807.M1P_GM204-200-A1_DSC04620_(29702898116).jpg)

Nvidia GeForce GTX 970 PCB and die

Issues with the GeForce GTX 970's specifications were first brought up by users when they found out that the cards, while featuring 4 GB of memory, rarely accessed memory over the 3.5 GB boundary. Further testing and investigation eventually led to Nvidia issuing a statement that the card's initially announced specifications had been altered without notice before the card was made commercially available, and that the card took a performance hit once memory over the 3.5 GB limit were put into use.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-106)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-107)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-108)

The card's back-end hardware specifications, initially announced as being identical to those of the GeForce GTX 980, differed in the amount of L2 cache (1.75 MB versus 2 MB in the GeForce GTX 980) and the number of ROPs (56 versus 64 in the 980). Additionally, it was revealed that the card was designed to access its memory as a 3.5 GB section, plus a 0.5 GB one, access to the latter being 7 times slower than the first one.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-109) The company then went on to promise a specific driver modification in order to alleviate the performance issues produced by the cutbacks suffered by the card.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-110) However, Nvidia later clarified that the promise had been a miscommunication and there would be no specific driver update for the GTX 970.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-111) Nvidia claimed that it would assist customers who wanted refunds in obtaining them.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-112) On February 26, 2015, Nvidia CEO Jen-Hsun Huang went on record in Nvidia's official blog to apologize for the incident.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-113) In February 2015 a class-action lawsuit alleging false advertising was filed against Nvidia and Gigabyte Technology in the U.S. District Court for Northern California.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-970lawsuit-114)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-115)

Nvidia revealed that it is able to disable individual units, each containing 256KB of L2 cache and 8 ROPs, without disabling whole memory controllers.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-AnandTechCorrectionPage2-116) This comes at the cost of dividing the memory bus into high speed and low speed segments that cannot be accessed at the same time unless one segment is reading while the other segment is writing because the L2/ROP unit managing both of the GDDR5 controllers shares the read return channel and the write data bus between the two GDDR5 controllers and itself.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-AnandTechCorrectionPage2-116) This is used in the GeForce GTX 970, which therefore can be described as having 3.5 GB in its high speed segment on a 224-bit bus and 0.5 GB in a low speed segment on a 32-bit bus.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-AnandTechCorrectionPage2-116)

On July 27, 2016, Nvidia agreed to a preliminary settlement of the U.S. class action lawsuit,[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-970lawsuit-114) offering a $30 refund on GTX 970 purchases. The agreed upon refund represents the portion of the cost of the storage and performance capabilities the consumers assumed they were obtaining when they purchased the card.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-117)

## Support

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Support")]

Driver 368.81 is the last driver to support Windows XP/Windows XP 64-bit.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

32-bit drivers for 32-bit operating systems were discontinued after the release of driver 391.35 in March 2018.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-118)

Notebook GPUs based on the [Kepler architecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kepler_architecture "Kepler architecture") moved to legacy support in April 2019 and stopped receiving critical security updates after April 2020.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-119)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-120) The Nvidia GeForce 910M and 920M from the 9xxM GPU family are affected by this change.

Nvidia announced that after the release of the 470 driver branch, it would transition driver support for the [Windows 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_7 "Windows 7") and [Windows 8.1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_8.1 "Windows 8.1") operating systems to legacy status and continue to provide critical security updates for these operating systems through September 2024.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-121)

In December 2025, Nvidia discontinued Game Ready Driver support for the Maxwell, Pascal, and Volta architectures, which includes the GeForce 900 series. Security updates are scheduled to be continued until October 2028, as per Nvidia.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-122)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-123) On July 1, 2025, Nvidia announced that driver branch 580 will be the last to support these architectures.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-124)

The **GeForce 900 series** is a family of [graphics processing units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphics_processing_unit "Graphics processing unit") developed by [Nvidia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia "Nvidia"), succeeding the [GeForce 700 series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_700_series "GeForce 700 series") and serving as the high-end introduction to the [Maxwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxwell_(microarchitecture) "Maxwell (microarchitecture)") microarchitecture, named after [James Clerk Maxwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Clerk_Maxwell "James Clerk Maxwell"). They were produced with [TSMC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TSMC "TSMC")'s [28 nm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/28_nm_process "28 nm process") process.

With Maxwell, the successor to [Kepler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kepler_(microarchitecture) "Kepler (microarchitecture)"), Nvidia expected three major outcomes: improved graphics capabilities, simplified programming, and better [energy efficiency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy_efficiency_(physics) "Energy efficiency (physics)") compared to the [GeForce 700 series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_700_series "GeForce 700 series") and [GeForce 600 series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_600_series "GeForce 600 series").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-Xbitlabs-9)

Maxwell was announced in September 2010,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-10) with the first Maxwell-based GeForce consumer-class products released in early 2014.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-11)

## Architecture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Architecture")]

Main article: [Maxwell (microarchitecture)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxwell_(microarchitecture) "Maxwell (microarchitecture)")

### First generation Maxwell (GM10x)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: First generation Maxwell (GM10x)")]

First generation [Maxwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxwell_(microarchitecture) "Maxwell (microarchitecture)") GM107/GM108 were released as GeForce GTX 745, GTX 750/750 Ti and GTX 850M/860M (GM107) and GT 830M/840M (GM108). These new chips provide few consumer-facing additional features; Nvidia instead focused on power efficiency. Nvidia increased the amount of L2 cache from 256 KiB on GK107 to 2 MiB on GM107, reducing the memory bandwidth needed. Accordingly, Nvidia cut the memory bus from 192 bit on GK106 to 128 bit on GM107, further saving power.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-anand750-12) Nvidia also changed the streaming multiprocessor design from that of Kepler (SMX), naming it SMM. The structure of the warp scheduler is inherited from Kepler, which allows each scheduler to issue up to two instructions that are independent from each other and are in order from the same warp. The layout of SMM units is partitioned so that each of the 4 warp schedulers in an SMM controls 1 set of 32 FP32 CUDA cores, 1 set of 8 load/store units, and 1 set of 8 special function units. This is in contrast to Kepler, where each SMX has 4 schedulers that schedule to a shared pool of 6 sets of 32 FP32 CUDA cores, 2 sets of 16 load/store units, and 2 sets of 16 special function units.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-AnandTechGTX750-13) These units are connected by a crossbar that uses power to allow the resources to be shared.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-AnandTechGTX750-13) This crossbar is removed in Maxwell.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-AnandTechGTX750-13) Texture units and FP64 CUDA cores are still shared.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-anand750-12) SMM allows for a finer-grain allocation of resources than SMX, saving power when the workload isn't optimal for shared resources. Nvidia claims a 128 CUDA core SMM has 86% of the performance of a 192 CUDA core SMX.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-anand750-12) Also, each Graphics Processing Cluster, or GPC, contains up to 4 SMX units in Kepler, and up to 5 SMM units in first generation Maxwell.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-anand750-12)

GM107 supports [CUDA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CUDA "CUDA") Compute Capability 5.0 compared to 3.5 on GK110/GK208 GPUs and 3.0 on GK10x GPUs. Dynamic Parallelism and HyperQ, two features in GK110/GK208 GPUs, are also supported across the entire Maxwell product line.

Maxwell provides native shared memory atomic operations for 32-bit integers and native shared memory 32-bit and 64-bit compare-and-swap (CAS), which can be used to implement other atomic functions.

While it was once thought that Maxwell used [tile-based immediate mode rasterization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiled_rendering "Tiled rendering"),[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-14) Nvidia corrected this at GDC 2017 saying Maxwell instead uses Tile Caching.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-15)

#### NVENC

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: NVENC")]

Main article: [Nvidia NVENC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia_NVENC "Nvidia NVENC")

Maxwell-based GPUs also contain the NVENC SIP block introduced with Kepler. Nvidia's video encoder, NVENC, is 1.5 to 2 times faster than on Kepler-based GPUs meaning it can encode video at 6 to 8 times playback speed.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-anand750-12)

#### PureVideo

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: PureVideo")]

Main article: [Nvidia PureVideo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia_PureVideo "Nvidia PureVideo")

Nvidia also claims an 8 to 10 times performance increase in [PureVideo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia_PureVideo "Nvidia PureVideo") Feature Set E video decoding due to the video decoder cache paired with increases in memory efficiency. However, [H.265](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H.265 "H.265") is not supported for full hardware decoding, relying on a mix of hardware and software decoding.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-anand750-12) When decoding video, a new low power state "GC5" is used on Maxwell GPUs to conserve power.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-anand750-12)

### Second generation Maxwell (GM20x)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Second generation Maxwell (GM20x)")]

Second generation Maxwell introduced several new technologies: Dynamic Super Resolution,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-16) Third Generation Delta Color Compression,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-international.download.nvidia.com-17) Multi-Pixel Programming Sampling,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-18) Nvidia VXGI (Real-Time-Voxel-[Global Illumination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_illumination "Global illumination")),[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-19) VR Direct,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-20)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-21)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-anandtech.com-22) Multi-Projection Acceleration,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-international.download.nvidia.com-17) and Multi-Frame Sampled Anti-Aliasing (MFAA)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-23) (however support for Coverage-Sampling Anti-Aliasing (CSAA) was removed).[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-24) HDMI 2.0 support was also added.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-25)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-26)

Second generation Maxwell also changed the ROP to memory controller ratio from 8:1 to 16:1.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-AnandTech980page3-27) However, some of the ROPs are generally idle in the GTX 970 because there are not enough enabled SMMs to give them work to do and therefore reduces its maximum fill rate.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-techreport.com-28)

Second generation upgraded [NVENC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NVENC "NVENC") which supports [HEVC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HEVC "HEVC") encoding and adds support for [H.264](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H.264 "H.264") encoding resolutions at 1440p/60FPS & 4K/60FPS compared to NVENC on Maxwell first generation GM10x GPUs which only supported H.264 1080p/60FPS encoding.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-anandtech.com-22) Maxwell GM206 GPU supports full fixed function HEVC hardware decoding.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-29)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-30)

### Async compute support

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Async compute support")]

While the Maxwell series was marketed as fully [DirectX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DirectX "DirectX") 12 compliant,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-dx12_1-2)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-980tidx12-31)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-auto-32) Oxide Games, developer of _[Ashes of the Singularity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashes\_of\_the\_Singularity "Ashes of the Singularity")_, uncovered that Maxwell-based cards do not perform well when async compute is utilized.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-33)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-oxidedx12-34)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-nvidiashim-35)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-980tidx12-31)

It appears that while this core feature is in fact exposed by the driver,[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-36) Nvidia partially implemented it through a driver-based [shim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shim_(computing) "Shim (computing)"), coming at a high performance cost.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-nvidiashim-35) Unlike AMD's competing [GCN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphics_Core_Next "Graphics Core Next")-based graphics cards which include a full implementation of hardware-based asynchronous compute,[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-37)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-38) Nvidia planned to rely on the driver to implement a software queue and a software distributor to forward asynchronous tasks to the hardware schedulers, capable of distributing the workload to the correct units.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-39) Asynchronous compute on Maxwell therefore requires that both a game and the GPU driver be specifically coded for asynchronous compute on Maxwell in order to enable this capability.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-PCPerTimeSpy-40) The 3DMark Time Spy benchmark shows no noticeable performance difference between asynchronous compute being enabled or disabled.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-PCPerTimeSpy-40) Asynchronous compute is disabled by the driver for Maxwell.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-PCPerTimeSpy-40)

Oxide claims that this led to Nvidia pressuring them not to include the asynchronous compute feature in their benchmark at all, so that the 900 series would not be at a disadvantage against AMD's products which implement asynchronous compute in hardware.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-oxidedx12-34)

Maxwell requires that the GPU be statically partitioned for asynchronous compute to allow tasks to run concurrently.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-RyanSmithDynamicScheduling-41) Each partition is assigned to a hardware queue. If any of the queues that are assigned to a partition empty out or are unable to submit work for any reason (e.g. a task in the queue must be delayed until a [hazard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hazard_(computer_architecture) "Hazard (computer architecture)") is resolved), the partition and all of the resources in that partition reserved for that queue will idle.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-RyanSmithDynamicScheduling-41) Asynchronous compute therefore could easily hurt performance on Maxwell if it is not coded to work with Maxwell's static scheduler.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-RyanSmithDynamicScheduling-41) Furthermore, graphics tasks saturate Nvidia GPUs much more easily than they do to AMD's GCN-based GPUs which are much more heavily weighted towards compute, so Nvidia GPUs have fewer scheduling holes that could be filled by asynchronous compute than AMD's.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-RyanSmithDynamicScheduling-41) For these reasons, the driver forces a Maxwell GPU to place all tasks into one queue and execute each task in serial, and give each task the undivided resources of the GPU no matter whether or not each task can saturate the GPU or not.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-RyanSmithDynamicScheduling-41)

## Advertising controversy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Advertising controversy")]

### GTX 970 hardware specifications

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: GTX 970 hardware specifications")]

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fb/NVIDIA%4028nm%40Maxwell%40GM204%40GeForce_GTX_970%40S_TAIWAN_1433A1_T4N807.M1P_GM204-200-A1_DSC04620_%2829702898116%29.jpg/250px-NVIDIA%4028nm%40Maxwell%40GM204%40GeForce_GTX_970%40S_TAIWAN_1433A1_T4N807.M1P_GM204-200-A1_DSC04620_%2829702898116%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:NVIDIA@28nm@Maxwell@GM204@GeForce_GTX_970@S_TAIWAN_1433A1_T4N807.M1P_GM204-200-A1_DSC04620_(29702898116).jpg)

Nvidia GeForce GTX 970 PCB and die

Issues with the GeForce GTX 970's specifications were first brought up by users when they found out that the cards, while featuring 4 GB of memory, rarely accessed memory over the 3.5 GB boundary. Further testing and investigation eventually led to Nvidia issuing a statement that the card's initially announced specifications had been altered without notice before the card was made commercially available, and that the card took a performance hit once memory over the 3.5 GB limit were put into use.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-106)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-107)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-108)

The card's back-end hardware specifications, initially announced as being identical to those of the GeForce GTX 980, differed in the amount of L2 cache (1.75 MB versus 2 MB in the GeForce GTX 980) and the number of ROPs (56 versus 64 in the 980). Additionally, it was revealed that the card was designed to access its memory as a 3.5 GB section, plus a 0.5 GB one, access to the latter being 7 times slower than the first one.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-109) The company then went on to promise a specific driver modification in order to alleviate the performance issues produced by the cutbacks suffered by the card.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-110) However, Nvidia later clarified that the promise had been a miscommunication and there would be no specific driver update for the GTX 970.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-111) Nvidia claimed that it would assist customers who wanted refunds in obtaining them.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-112) On February 26, 2015, Nvidia CEO Jen-Hsun Huang went on record in Nvidia's official blog to apologize for the incident.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-113) In February 2015 a class-action lawsuit alleging false advertising was filed against Nvidia and Gigabyte Technology in the U.S. District Court for Northern California.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-970lawsuit-114)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-115)

Nvidia revealed that it is able to disable individual units, each containing 256KB of L2 cache and 8 ROPs, without disabling whole memory controllers.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-AnandTechCorrectionPage2-116) This comes at the cost of dividing the memory bus into high speed and low speed segments that cannot be accessed at the same time unless one segment is reading while the other segment is writing because the L2/ROP unit managing both of the GDDR5 controllers shares the read return channel and the write data bus between the two GDDR5 controllers and itself.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-AnandTechCorrectionPage2-116) This is used in the GeForce GTX 970, which therefore can be described as having 3.5 GB in its high speed segment on a 224-bit bus and 0.5 GB in a low speed segment on a 32-bit bus.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-AnandTechCorrectionPage2-116)

On July 27, 2016, Nvidia agreed to a preliminary settlement of the U.S. class action lawsuit,[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-970lawsuit-114) offering a $30 refund on GTX 970 purchases. The agreed upon refund represents the portion of the cost of the storage and performance capabilities the consumers assumed they were obtaining when they purchased the card.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-117)

## Support

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Support")]

Driver 368.81 is the last driver to support Windows XP/Windows XP 64-bit.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

32-bit drivers for 32-bit operating systems were discontinued after the release of driver 391.35 in March 2018.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-118)

Notebook GPUs based on the [Kepler architecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kepler_architecture "Kepler architecture") moved to legacy support in April 2019 and stopped receiving critical security updates after April 2020.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-119)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-120) The Nvidia GeForce 910M and 920M from the 9xxM GPU family are affected by this change.

Nvidia announced that after the release of the 470 driver branch, it would transition driver support for the [Windows 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_7 "Windows 7") and [Windows 8.1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_8.1 "Windows 8.1") operating systems to legacy status and continue to provide critical security updates for these operating systems through September 2024.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-121)

In December 2025, Nvidia discontinued Game Ready Driver support for the Maxwell, Pascal, and Volta architectures, which includes the GeForce 900 series. Security updates are scheduled to be continued until October 2028, as per Nvidia.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-122)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-123) On July 1, 2025, Nvidia announced that driver branch 580 will be the last to support these architectures.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_900_series#cite_note-124)

The **GeForce 900 series** is a family of [graphics processing units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphics_processing_unit "Graphics processing unit") developed by [Nvidia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia "Nvidia"), succeeding the [GeForce 700 series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_700_series "GeForce 700 series") and serving as the high-end introduction to the [Maxwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxwell_(microarchitecture) "Maxwell (microarchitecture)") microarchitecture, named after [James Clerk Maxwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Clerk_Maxwell "James Clerk Maxwell"). They were produced with [TSMC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TSMC "TSMC")'s [28 nm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/28_nm_process "28 nm process") process.

With Maxwell, the successor to [Kepler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kepler_(microarchitecture) "Kepler (microarchitecture)"), Nvidia expected three major outcomes: improved graphics capabilities, simplified programming, and better [energy efficiency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy_efficiency_(physics) "Energy efficiency (physics)") compared to the [GeForce 700 series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_700_series "GeForce 700 series") and [GeForce 600 series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_600_series "GeForce 600 series").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-Xbitlabs-9)

Maxwell was announced in September 2010,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-10) with the first Maxwell-based GeForce consumer-class products released in early 2014.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-11)

## Architecture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Architecture")]

Main article: [Maxwell (microarchitecture)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxwell_(microarchitecture) "Maxwell (microarchitecture)")

### First generation Maxwell (GM10x)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: First generation Maxwell (GM10x)")]

First generation [Maxwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxwell_(microarchitecture) "Maxwell (microarchitecture)") GM107/GM108 were released as GeForce GTX 745, GTX 750/750 Ti and GTX 850M/860M (GM107) and GT 830M/840M (GM108). These new chips provide few consumer-facing additional features; Nvidia instead focused on power efficiency. Nvidia increased the amount of L2 cache from 256 KiB on GK107 to 2 MiB on GM107, reducing the memory bandwidth needed. Accordingly, Nvidia cut the memory bus from 192 bit on GK106 to 128 bit on GM107, further saving power.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-anand750-12) Nvidia also changed the streaming multiprocessor design from that of Kepler (SMX), naming it SMM. The structure of the warp scheduler is inherited from Kepler, which allows each scheduler to issue up to two instructions that are independent from each other and are in order from the same warp. The layout of SMM units is partitioned so that each of the 4 warp schedulers in an SMM controls 1 set of 32 FP32 CUDA cores, 1 set of 8 load/store units, and 1 set of 8 special function units. This is in contrast to Kepler, where each SMX has 4 schedulers that schedule to a shared pool of 6 sets of 32 FP32 CUDA cores, 2 sets of 16 load/store units, and 2 sets of 16 special function units.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-AnandTechGTX750-13) These units are connected by a crossbar that uses power to allow the resources to be shared.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-AnandTechGTX750-13) This crossbar is removed in Maxwell.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-AnandTechGTX750-13) Texture units and FP64 CUDA cores are still shared.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-anand750-12) SMM allows for a finer-grain allocation of resources than SMX, saving power when the workload isn't optimal for shared resources. Nvidia claims a 128 CUDA core SMM has 86% of the performance of a 192 CUDA core SMX.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-anand750-12) Also, each Graphics Processing Cluster, or GPC, contains up to 4 SMX units in Kepler, and up to 5 SMM units in first generation Maxwell.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-anand750-12)

GM107 supports [CUDA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CUDA "CUDA") Compute Capability 5.0 compared to 3.5 on GK110/GK208 GPUs and 3.0 on GK10x GPUs. Dynamic Parallelism and HyperQ, two features in GK110/GK208 GPUs, are also supported across the entire Maxwell product line.

Maxwell provides native shared memory atomic operations for 32-bit integers and native shared memory 32-bit and 64-bit compare-and-swap (CAS), which can be used to implement other atomic functions.

While it was once thought that Maxwell used [tile-based immediate mode rasterization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiled_rendering "Tiled rendering"),[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-14) Nvidia corrected this at GDC 2017 saying Maxwell instead uses Tile Caching.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-15)

#### NVENC

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: NVENC")]

Main article: [Nvidia NVENC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia_NVENC "Nvidia NVENC")

Maxwell-based GPUs also contain the NVENC SIP block introduced with Kepler. Nvidia's video encoder, NVENC, is 1.5 to 2 times faster than on Kepler-based GPUs meaning it can encode video at 6 to 8 times playback speed.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-anand750-12)

#### PureVideo

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: PureVideo")]

Main article: [Nvidia PureVideo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia_PureVideo "Nvidia PureVideo")

Nvidia also claims an 8 to 10 times performance increase in [PureVideo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia_PureVideo "Nvidia PureVideo") Feature Set E video decoding due to the video decoder cache paired with increases in memory efficiency. However, [H.265](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H.265 "H.265") is not supported for full hardware decoding, relying on a mix of hardware and software decoding.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-anand750-12) When decoding video, a new low power state "GC5" is used on Maxwell GPUs to conserve power.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-anand750-12)

### Second generation Maxwell (GM20x)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Second generation Maxwell (GM20x)")]

Second generation Maxwell introduced several new technologies: Dynamic Super Resolution,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-16) Third Generation Delta Color Compression,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-international.download.nvidia.com-17) Multi-Pixel Programming Sampling,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-18) Nvidia VXGI (Real-Time-Voxel-[Global Illumination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_illumination "Global illumination")),[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-19) VR Direct,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-20)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-21)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-anandtech.com-22) Multi-Projection Acceleration,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-international.download.nvidia.com-17) and Multi-Frame Sampled Anti-Aliasing (MFAA)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-23) (however support for Coverage-Sampling Anti-Aliasing (CSAA) was removed).[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-24) HDMI 2.0 support was also added.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-25)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-26)

Second generation Maxwell also changed the ROP to memory controller ratio from 8:1 to 16:1.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-AnandTech980page3-27) However, some of the ROPs are generally idle in the GTX 970 because there are not enough enabled SMMs to give them work to do and therefore reduces its maximum fill rate.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-techreport.com-28)

Second generation upgraded [NVENC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NVENC "NVENC") which supports [HEVC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HEVC "HEVC") encoding and adds support for [H.264](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H.264 "H.264") encoding resolutions at 1440p/60FPS & 4K/60FPS compared to NVENC on Maxwell first generation GM10x GPUs which only supported H.264 1080p/60FPS encoding.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-anandtech.com-22) Maxwell GM206 GPU supports full fixed function HEVC hardware decoding.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-29)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-30)

### Async compute support

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Async compute support")]

While the Maxwell series was marketed as fully [DirectX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DirectX "DirectX") 12 compliant,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-dx12_1-2)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-980tidx12-31)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-auto-32) Oxide Games, developer of _[Ashes of the Singularity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashes\_of\_the\_Singularity "Ashes of the Singularity")_, uncovered that Maxwell-based cards do not perform well when async compute is utilized.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-33)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-oxidedx12-34)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-nvidiashim-35)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-980tidx12-31)

It appears that while this core feature is in fact exposed by the driver,[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-36) Nvidia partially implemented it through a driver-based [shim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shim_(computing) "Shim (computing)"), coming at a high performance cost.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-nvidiashim-35) Unlike AMD's competing [GCN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphics_Core_Next "Graphics Core Next")-based graphics cards which include a full implementation of hardware-based asynchronous compute,[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-37)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-38) Nvidia planned to rely on the driver to implement a software queue and a software distributor to forward asynchronous tasks to the hardware schedulers, capable of distributing the workload to the correct units.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-39) Asynchronous compute on Maxwell therefore requires that both a game and the GPU driver be specifically coded for asynchronous compute on Maxwell in order to enable this capability.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-PCPerTimeSpy-40) The 3DMark Time Spy benchmark shows no noticeable performance difference between asynchronous compute being enabled or disabled.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-PCPerTimeSpy-40) Asynchronous compute is disabled by the driver for Maxwell.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-PCPerTimeSpy-40)

Oxide claims that this led to Nvidia pressuring them not to include the asynchronous compute feature in their benchmark at all, so that the 900 series would not be at a disadvantage against AMD's products which implement asynchronous compute in hardware.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-oxidedx12-34)

Maxwell requires that the GPU be statically partitioned for asynchronous compute to allow tasks to run concurrently.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-RyanSmithDynamicScheduling-41) Each partition is assigned to a hardware queue. If any of the queues that are assigned to a partition empty out or are unable to submit work for any reason (e.g. a task in the queue must be delayed until a [hazard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hazard_(computer_architecture) "Hazard (computer architecture)") is resolved), the partition and all of the resources in that partition reserved for that queue will idle.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-RyanSmithDynamicScheduling-41) Asynchronous compute therefore could easily hurt performance on Maxwell if it is not coded to work with Maxwell's static scheduler.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-RyanSmithDynamicScheduling-41) Furthermore, graphics tasks saturate Nvidia GPUs much more easily than they do to AMD's GCN-based GPUs which are much more heavily weighted towards compute, so Nvidia GPUs have fewer scheduling holes that could be filled by asynchronous compute than AMD's.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-RyanSmithDynamicScheduling-41) For these reasons, the driver forces a Maxwell GPU to place all tasks into one queue and execute each task in serial, and give each task the undivided resources of the GPU no matter whether or not each task can saturate the GPU or not.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-RyanSmithDynamicScheduling-41)

## Advertising controversy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Advertising controversy")]

### GTX 970 hardware specifications

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: GTX 970 hardware specifications")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fb/NVIDIA%4028nm%40Maxwell%40GM204%40GeForce_GTX_970%40S_TAIWAN_1433A1_T4N807.M1P_GM204-200-A1_DSC04620_%2829702898116%29.jpg/250px-NVIDIA%4028nm%40Maxwell%40GM204%40GeForce_GTX_970%40S_TAIWAN_1433A1_T4N807.M1P_GM204-200-A1_DSC04620_%2829702898116%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:NVIDIA@28nm@Maxwell@GM204@GeForce_GTX_970@S_TAIWAN_1433A1_T4N807.M1P_GM204-200-A1_DSC04620_(29702898116).jpg)

Nvidia GeForce GTX 970 PCB and die

Issues with the GeForce GTX 970's specifications were first brought up by users when they found out that the cards, while featuring 4 GB of memory, rarely accessed memory over the 3.5 GB boundary. Further testing and investigation eventually led to Nvidia issuing a statement that the card's initially announced specifications had been altered without notice before the card was made commercially available, and that the card took a performance hit once memory over the 3.5 GB limit were put into use.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-106)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-107)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-108)

The card's back-end hardware specifications, initially announced as being identical to those of the GeForce GTX 980, differed in the amount of L2 cache (1.75 MB versus 2 MB in the GeForce GTX 980) and the number of ROPs (56 versus 64 in the 980). Additionally, it was revealed that the card was designed to access its memory as a 3.5 GB section, plus a 0.5 GB one, access to the latter being 7 times slower than the first one.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-109) The company then went on to promise a specific driver modification in order to alleviate the performance issues produced by the cutbacks suffered by the card.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-110) However, Nvidia later clarified that the promise had been a miscommunication and there would be no specific driver update for the GTX 970.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-111) Nvidia claimed that it would assist customers who wanted refunds in obtaining them.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-112) On February 26, 2015, Nvidia CEO Jen-Hsun Huang went on record in Nvidia's official blog to apologize for the incident.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-113) In February 2015 a class-action lawsuit alleging false advertising was filed against Nvidia and Gigabyte Technology in the U.S. District Court for Northern California.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-970lawsuit-114)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-115)

Nvidia revealed that it is able to disable individual units, each containing 256KB of L2 cache and 8 ROPs, without disabling whole memory controllers.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-AnandTechCorrectionPage2-116) This comes at the cost of dividing the memory bus into high speed and low speed segments that cannot be accessed at the same time unless one segment is reading while the other segment is writing because the L2/ROP unit managing both of the GDDR5 controllers shares the read return channel and the write data bus between the two GDDR5 controllers and itself.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-AnandTechCorrectionPage2-116) This is used in the GeForce GTX 970, which therefore can be described as having 3.5 GB in its high speed segment on a 224-bit bus and 0.5 GB in a low speed segment on a 32-bit bus.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-AnandTechCorrectionPage2-116)

On July 27, 2016, Nvidia agreed to a preliminary settlement of the U.S. class action lawsuit,[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-970lawsuit-114) offering a $30 refund on GTX 970 purchases. The agreed upon refund represents the portion of the cost of the storage and performance capabilities the consumers assumed they were obtaining when they purchased the card.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-117)

## Support

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Support")]

Driver 368.81 is the last driver to support Windows XP/Windows XP 64-bit.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

32-bit drivers for 32-bit operating systems were discontinued after the release of driver 391.35 in March 2018.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-118)

Notebook GPUs based on the [Kepler architecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kepler_architecture "Kepler architecture") moved to legacy support in April 2019 and stopped receiving critical security updates after April 2020.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-119)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-120) The Nvidia GeForce 910M and 920M from the 9xxM GPU family are affected by this change.

Nvidia announced that after the release of the 470 driver branch, it would transition driver support for the [Windows 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_7 "Windows 7") and [Windows 8.1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_8.1 "Windows 8.1") operating systems to legacy status and continue to provide critical security updates for these operating systems through September 2024.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-121)

In December 2025, Nvidia discontinued Game Ready Driver support for the Maxwell, Pascal, and Volta architectures, which includes the GeForce 900 series. Security updates are scheduled to be continued until October 2028, as per Nvidia.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-122)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-123) On July 1, 2025, Nvidia announced that driver branch 580 will be the last to support these architectures.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-124)

The **GeForce 900 series** is a family of [graphics processing units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphics_processing_unit "Graphics processing unit") developed by [Nvidia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia "Nvidia"), succeeding the [GeForce 700 series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_700_series "GeForce 700 series") and serving as the high-end introduction to the [Maxwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxwell_(microarchitecture) "Maxwell (microarchitecture)") microarchitecture, named after [James Clerk Maxwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Clerk_Maxwell "James Clerk Maxwell"). They were produced with [TSMC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TSMC "TSMC")'s [28 nm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/28_nm_process "28 nm process") process.

With Maxwell, the successor to [Kepler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kepler_(microarchitecture) "Kepler (microarchitecture)"), Nvidia expected three major outcomes: improved graphics capabilities, simplified programming, and better [energy efficiency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy_efficiency_(physics) "Energy efficiency (physics)") compared to the [GeForce 700 series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_700_series "GeForce 700 series") and [GeForce 600 series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_600_series "GeForce 600 series").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-Xbitlabs-9)

Maxwell was announced in September 2010,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-10) with the first Maxwell-based GeForce consumer-class products released in early 2014.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-11)

## Architecture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Architecture")]

Main article: [Maxwell (microarchitecture)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxwell_(microarchitecture) "Maxwell (microarchitecture)")

### First generation Maxwell (GM10x)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: First generation Maxwell (GM10x)")]

First generation [Maxwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxwell_(microarchitecture) "Maxwell (microarchitecture)") GM107/GM108 were released as GeForce GTX 745, GTX 750/750 Ti and GTX 850M/860M (GM107) and GT 830M/840M (GM108). These new chips provide few consumer-facing additional features; Nvidia instead focused on power efficiency. Nvidia increased the amount of L2 cache from 256 KiB on GK107 to 2 MiB on GM107, reducing the memory bandwidth needed. Accordingly, Nvidia cut the memory bus from 192 bit on GK106 to 128 bit on GM107, further saving power.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-anand750-12) Nvidia also changed the streaming multiprocessor design from that of Kepler (SMX), naming it SMM. The structure of the warp scheduler is inherited from Kepler, which allows each scheduler to issue up to two instructions that are independent from each other and are in order from the same warp. The layout of SMM units is partitioned so that each of the 4 warp schedulers in an SMM controls 1 set of 32 FP32 CUDA cores, 1 set of 8 load/store units, and 1 set of 8 special function units. This is in contrast to Kepler, where each SMX has 4 schedulers that schedule to a shared pool of 6 sets of 32 FP32 CUDA cores, 2 sets of 16 load/store units, and 2 sets of 16 special function units.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-AnandTechGTX750-13) These units are connected by a crossbar that uses power to allow the resources to be shared.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-AnandTechGTX750-13) This crossbar is removed in Maxwell.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-AnandTechGTX750-13) Texture units and FP64 CUDA cores are still shared.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-anand750-12) SMM allows for a finer-grain allocation of resources than SMX, saving power when the workload isn't optimal for shared resources. Nvidia claims a 128 CUDA core SMM has 86% of the performance of a 192 CUDA core SMX.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-anand750-12) Also, each Graphics Processing Cluster, or GPC, contains up to 4 SMX units in Kepler, and up to 5 SMM units in first generation Maxwell.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-anand750-12)

GM107 supports [CUDA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CUDA "CUDA") Compute Capability 5.0 compared to 3.5 on GK110/GK208 GPUs and 3.0 on GK10x GPUs. Dynamic Parallelism and HyperQ, two features in GK110/GK208 GPUs, are also supported across the entire Maxwell product line.

Maxwell provides native shared memory atomic operations for 32-bit integers and native shared memory 32-bit and 64-bit compare-and-swap (CAS), which can be used to implement other atomic functions.

While it was once thought that Maxwell used [tile-based immediate mode rasterization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiled_rendering "Tiled rendering"),[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-14) Nvidia corrected this at GDC 2017 saying Maxwell instead uses Tile Caching.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-15)

#### NVENC

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: NVENC")]

Main article: [Nvidia NVENC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia_NVENC "Nvidia NVENC")

Maxwell-based GPUs also contain the NVENC SIP block introduced with Kepler. Nvidia's video encoder, NVENC, is 1.5 to 2 times faster than on Kepler-based GPUs meaning it can encode video at 6 to 8 times playback speed.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-anand750-12)

#### PureVideo

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: PureVideo")]

Main article: [Nvidia PureVideo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia_PureVideo "Nvidia PureVideo")

Nvidia also claims an 8 to 10 times performance increase in [PureVideo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia_PureVideo "Nvidia PureVideo") Feature Set E video decoding due to the video decoder cache paired with increases in memory efficiency. However, [H.265](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H.265 "H.265") is not supported for full hardware decoding, relying on a mix of hardware and software decoding.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-anand750-12) When decoding video, a new low power state "GC5" is used on Maxwell GPUs to conserve power.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-anand750-12)

### Second generation Maxwell (GM20x)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Second generation Maxwell (GM20x)")]

Second generation Maxwell introduced several new technologies: Dynamic Super Resolution,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-16) Third Generation Delta Color Compression,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-international.download.nvidia.com-17) Multi-Pixel Programming Sampling,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-18) Nvidia VXGI (Real-Time-Voxel-[Global Illumination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_illumination "Global illumination")),[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-19) VR Direct,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-20)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-21)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-anandtech.com-22) Multi-Projection Acceleration,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-international.download.nvidia.com-17) and Multi-Frame Sampled Anti-Aliasing (MFAA)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-23) (however support for Coverage-Sampling Anti-Aliasing (CSAA) was removed).[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-24) HDMI 2.0 support was also added.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-25)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-26)

Second generation Maxwell also changed the ROP to memory controller ratio from 8:1 to 16:1.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-AnandTech980page3-27) However, some of the ROPs are generally idle in the GTX 970 because there are not enough enabled SMMs to give them work to do and therefore reduces its maximum fill rate.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-techreport.com-28)

Second generation upgraded [NVENC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NVENC "NVENC") which supports [HEVC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HEVC "HEVC") encoding and adds support for [H.264](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H.264 "H.264") encoding resolutions at 1440p/60FPS & 4K/60FPS compared to NVENC on Maxwell first generation GM10x GPUs which only supported H.264 1080p/60FPS encoding.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-anandtech.com-22) Maxwell GM206 GPU supports full fixed function HEVC hardware decoding.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-29)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-30)

### Async compute support

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_900_series&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Async compute support")]

While the Maxwell series was marketed as fully [DirectX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DirectX "DirectX") 12 compliant,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-dx12_1-2)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-980tidx12-31)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-auto-32) Oxide Games, developer of _[Ashes of the Singularity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashes\_of\_the\_Singularity "Ashes of the Singularity")_, uncovered that Maxwell-based cards do not perform well when async compute is utilized.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-33)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-oxidedx12-34)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-nvidiashim-35)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-980tidx12-31)

It appears that while this core feature is in fact exposed by the driver,[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-36) Nvidia partially implemented it through a driver-based [shim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shim_(computing) "Shim (computing)"), coming at a high performance cost.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-nvidiashim-35) Unlike AMD's competing [GCN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphics_Core_Next "Graphics Core Next")-based graphics cards which include a full implementation of hardware-based asynchronous compute,[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-37)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-38) Nvidia planned to rely on the driver to implement a software queue and a software distributor to forward asynchronous tasks to the hardware schedulers, capable of distributing the workload to the correct units.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-39) Asynchronous compute on Maxwell therefore requires that both a game and the GPU driver be specifically coded for asynchronous compute on Maxwell in order to enable this capability.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-PCPerTimeSpy-40) The 3DMark Time Spy benchmark shows no noticeable performance difference between asynchronous compute being enabled or disabled.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-PCPerTimeSpy-40) Asynchronous compute is disabled by the driver for Maxwell.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-PCPerTimeSpy-40)

Oxide claims that this led to Nvidia pressuring them not to include the asynchronous compute feature in their benchmark at all, so that the 900 series would not be at a disadvantage against AMD's products which implement asynchronous compute in hardware.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-oxidedx12-34)

Maxwell requires that the GPU be statically partitioned for asynchronous compute to allow tasks to run concurrently.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-RyanSmithDynamicScheduling-41) Each partition is assigned to a hardware queue. If any of the queues that are assigned to a partition empty out or are unable to submit work for any reason (e.g. a task in the queue must be delayed until a [hazard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hazard_(computer_architecture) "Hazard (computer architecture)") is resolved), the partition and all of the resources in that partition reserved for that queue will idle.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-RyanSmithDynamicScheduling-41) Asynchronous compute therefore could easily hurt performance on Maxwell if it is not coded to work with Maxwell's static scheduler.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-RyanSmithDynamicScheduling-41) Furthermore, graphics tasks saturate Nvidia GPUs much more easily than they do to AMD's GCN-based GPUs which are much more heavily weighted towards compute, so Nvidia GPUs have fewer scheduling holes that could be filled by asynchronous compute than AMD's.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-RyanSmithDynamicScheduling-41) For these reasons, the driver forces a Maxwell GPU to place all tasks into one queue and execute each task in serial, and give each task the undivided resources of the GPU no matter whether or not each task can saturate the GPU or not.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_970#cite_note-RyanSmithDynamicScheduling-41)
